stem: A change in which one or more new substances with new properties are formed is called a __________.
solution: A chemical reaction forms new substances with different properties.

stem: The substances that take part in a chemical reaction are called __________.
solution: Reactants are the starting substances that undergo change in a reaction.

stem: The new substances formed in a chemical reaction are called __________.
solution: Products are the new substances formed as a result of a chemical reaction.

stem: A balanced chemical equation obeys the law of __________.
solution: A balanced equation has equal atoms of each element on both sides, obeying conservation of mass.

stem: In a balanced chemical equation, the number of atoms of each element is __________ on both sides.
solution: Balancing ensures equal numbers of atoms of each element on the reactant and product sides.

stem: A reaction in which two or more substances combine to form a single product is a __________ reaction.
solution: In a combination reaction, two or more reactants form a single product.

stem: A reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances is a __________ reaction.
solution: In a decomposition reaction, a single compound splits into two or more products.

stem: A decomposition reaction that uses heat is called __________ decomposition.
solution: Thermal decomposition uses heat to break down a compound, e.g., decomposition of calcium carbonate.

stem: A decomposition reaction carried out using electricity is called __________.
solution: Electrolytic decomposition (electrolysis) breaks down a compound using electric current, e.g., electrolysis of water.

stem: The decomposition of silver chloride to silver and chlorine in sunlight is an example of __________.
solution: Silver chloride decomposes in light (photodecomposition), which is used in black-and-white photography.

stem: A reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound is a __________ reaction.
solution: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element replaces a less reactive one from its compound.

stem: When iron is added to copper sulphate solution, iron displaces copper because iron is __________ than copper.
solution: Iron, being more reactive than copper, displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.

stem: A reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds is a __________ reaction.
solution: In a double displacement reaction, ions are exchanged between two compounds.

stem: The formation of an insoluble solid when two solutions are mixed is called a __________.
solution: A precipitate is an insoluble solid formed in a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.

stem: A reaction in which heat is released is called an __________ reaction.
solution: Exothermic reactions release heat energy.

stem: A reaction in which heat is absorbed is called an __________ reaction.
solution: Endothermic reactions absorb heat energy from the surroundings.

stem: The burning of fuels and respiration are examples of __________ reactions.
solution: Combustion and respiration release energy, so they are exothermic reactions.

stem: The gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen by a substance is called __________.
solution: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen during a reaction.

stem: The loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen by a substance is called __________.
solution: Reduction is the loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen.

stem: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction occur together is called a __________ reaction.
solution: A redox reaction involves simultaneous oxidation and reduction.

stem: The slow eating away of a metal by the action of air and moisture is called __________.
solution: Corrosion is the gradual deterioration of a metal by reaction with air, moisture and chemicals.

stem: The reddish-brown coating formed on iron due to corrosion is called __________.
solution: Rust (hydrated iron oxide) is the reddish-brown coating formed when iron corrodes.

stem: The slow oxidation of fats and oils in food, giving an unpleasant smell and taste, is called __________.
solution: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats/oils in food, spoiling its taste and smell.

stem: Rancidity can be prevented by adding substances called __________ to food.
solution: Antioxidants prevent the oxidation of fats and oils, slowing rancidity.

stem: Packing food in nitrogen gas prevents rancidity because nitrogen __________.
solution: Nitrogen is unreactive and displaces oxygen, preventing the oxidation that causes rancidity.

stem: The reaction Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2 is an example of a __________ reaction.
solution: Zinc displaces hydrogen from sulphuric acid, a displacement reaction.

stem: The burning of magnesium ribbon in air is a __________ reaction.
solution: Magnesium combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide — a combination reaction (and oxidation).

stem: The heating of limestone (CaCO3) to give lime (CaO) and carbon dioxide is a __________ reaction.
solution: CaCO3 decomposes on heating into CaO and CO2 — thermal decomposition.

stem: Which of the following prevents rusting of iron?
solution: Coatings like paint, oil or a zinc layer (galvanising) protect iron from rusting.

stem: In the reaction CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O, copper oxide is __________.
solution: CuO loses oxygen to form Cu, so it is reduced; hydrogen gains oxygen and is oxidised.

stem: A chemical equation is written with reactants on the __________ and products on the right.
solution: By convention, reactants are written on the left and products on the right of the arrow.

stem: The symbol (g), (l), (s) and (aq) in a chemical equation indicate the __________.
solution: These symbols show the physical states: gas, liquid, solid, and aqueous solution.

stem: The unbalanced equation must be __________ to satisfy the law of conservation of mass.
solution: Chemical equations are balanced so that atoms of each element are equal on both sides.

stem: The evolution of gas (bubbles) during a reaction is a sign of a __________.
solution: Gas evolution is one of the observable signs that a chemical reaction has occurred.

stem: When barium chloride reacts with sodium sulphate, a white precipitate of __________ forms.
solution: The double displacement reaction forms insoluble barium sulphate (white precipitate) and soluble sodium chloride.

stem: Which of the following is an endothermic process?
options: Decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating
solution: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate absorbs heat, making it endothermic.

stem: A silvery-white metal that burns in air with a dazzling white flame is __________.
solution: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, forming magnesium oxide.

stem: Chips packets are flushed with nitrogen mainly to __________.
options: prevent the oxidation (rancidity) of the food
solution: Nitrogen removes oxygen, preventing oxidation and rancidity of the fatty food.

stem: The colour change, gas formation, temperature change and precipitate formation are all signs of a __________.
solution: These observations indicate that a chemical reaction (forming new substances) has occurred.

stem: The reaction of quicklime (CaO) with water to form slaked lime, releasing heat, is a __________ reaction.
solution: CaO combines with water to form Ca(OH)2, releasing much heat — a combination and exothermic reaction.

stem: The green coating that forms on copper vessels in moist air is due to corrosion, forming __________.
solution: Copper corrodes in moist air to form a green coating of basic copper carbonate (verdigris).

stem: The black coating that tarnishes silver articles is due to the formation of __________.
solution: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air to form black silver sulphide (tarnish).

stem: The oxidising agent in a redox reaction is the substance that __________.
solution: An oxidising agent oxidises another substance and itself gets reduced.

stem: The reducing agent in a redox reaction is the substance that __________.
solution: A reducing agent reduces another substance and itself gets oxidised.

stem: Respiration is a chemical reaction that is __________.
solution: Respiration breaks down glucose to release energy, so it is an exothermic reaction.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a reaction type with an example?
solution: Hydrogen and oxygen combining to form water is a combination reaction.

stem: A photochemical reaction is one that is driven by __________.
solution: Photochemical reactions are driven by light, e.g., the decomposition of silver chloride and photosynthesis.

stem: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products is a __________ reaction.
solution: In a decomposition reaction, one compound breaks into two or more simpler substances.

stem: The gain of oxygen during a reaction is called __________.
solution: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen (or loss of hydrogen) by a substance.

stem: Rancidity is the oxidation of __________ in food.
solution: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, spoiling the taste and smell of food.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Chemical Reactions and Equations' is that:
options: chemical reactions form new substances, are represented by balanced equations, and occur as various types (combination, decomposition, displacement, redox) with effects like corrosion and rancidity
solution: The chapter explains chemical reactions, balancing equations (conservation of mass), types of reactions, oxidation-reduction, and corrosion and rancidity.

stem: In the reaction Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂, zinc is __________.
solution: Zinc loses electrons (its oxidation state rises from 0 to +2), so it is oxidised.

stem: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down into simpler products is a __________ reaction.
solution: In decomposition, one compound splits into two or more simpler substances.

stem: The decomposition of a substance using electricity is called __________.
solution: Electrolysis is decomposition brought about by passing electricity through a substance.

stem: The decomposition of silver chloride to silver and chlorine on exposure to sunlight is a __________ reaction.
solution: Light drives this decomposition, making it a photochemical (photolytic) reaction.

stem: When quicklime (CaO) reacts with water to form slaked lime, the reaction is __________.
solution: The reaction of CaO with water releases a large amount of heat, so it is exothermic.

stem: Respiration is considered a(n) __________ reaction because it releases energy.
solution: Respiration breaks down glucose and releases energy, so it is exothermic.

stem: The reaction Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu is a __________ reaction.
solution: The more reactive iron displaces copper from copper sulphate — a displacement reaction.

stem: In the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride, a white precipitate of __________ forms.
solution: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO₃; the white precipitate is silver chloride.

stem: A reaction in which two ions are exchanged between reactants forming a precipitate is a __________ reaction.
solution: Double displacement reactions involve the exchange of ions, often forming a precipitate.

stem: The black coating that forms on silver articles over time is due to __________.
solution: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air to form a black layer of silver sulphide (corrosion).

stem: The green coating on copper articles exposed to moist air is mainly __________.
solution: Copper corrodes to form a green layer of basic copper carbonate.

stem: The slow oxidation of fats and oils in food, spoiling their taste and smell, is called __________.
solution: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, giving foods an unpleasant taste and smell.

stem: Antioxidants are added to packaged food to __________.
solution: Antioxidants prevent the oxidation of fats and oils, delaying rancidity.

stem: Chips packets are flushed with __________ gas to prevent rancidity.
solution: Unreactive nitrogen replaces oxygen in chip packets, preventing oxidation and rancidity.

stem: A balanced chemical equation obeys the law of conservation of __________.
solution: A balanced equation has equal numbers of atoms on both sides, satisfying conservation of mass.

stem: The symbol '↓' written after a product in an equation indicates a __________.
solution: A downward arrow '↓' shows that the product is a precipitate that settles out.

stem: The symbol '↑' after a product in an equation indicates a __________.
solution: An upward arrow '↑' shows that the product is a gas released in the reaction.

stem: When dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide, the reaction is a __________.
solution: Acid and base neutralise to form salt and water — a double displacement (neutralisation) reaction.

stem: The reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O is best classified as a __________ reaction.
solution: Two elements combine to form a single compound (water), so it is a combination reaction.

stem: The burning of magnesium ribbon in air is an example of a __________ reaction.
solution: Magnesium combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide, releasing heat and light — combination, exothermic.

stem: Magnesium ribbon is cleaned before burning to remove the layer of __________.
solution: A protective magnesium oxide layer is cleaned off so the ribbon burns readily.

stem: In the thermite reaction, aluminium displaces iron from iron oxide; this is a __________ reaction.
solution: Aluminium displaces iron, releasing enough heat to weld iron — a highly exothermic displacement reaction.

stem: A substance that gets oxidised is called the __________ agent.
solution: The substance that is oxidised reduces the other, so it is the reducing agent.

stem: A substance that gets reduced is called the __________ agent.
solution: The substance that is reduced oxidises the other, so it is the oxidising agent.

stem: When ferrous sulphate crystals are heated, they lose water and change colour to __________.
solution: Heating FeSO₄ decomposes it, producing reddish-brown ferric oxide along with gases.

stem: Digestion of food in the body is a __________ reaction.
solution: Large food molecules break down into simpler ones, so digestion is a decomposition process.

stem: The rusting of iron requires both __________.
solution: Iron rusts only in the presence of both oxygen and water (moisture).

stem: The heating of limestone (CaCO₃) to give quicklime and carbon dioxide is a __________ reaction.
solution: CaCO₃ decomposes on heating into CaO and CO₂ — an endothermic thermal decomposition.

stem: In a chemical equation, the numbers placed before formulae to balance it are called __________.
solution: Coefficients are the balancing numbers written before formulae in an equation.

stem: The reaction of an acid with a metal generally releases __________ gas.
solution: Metals react with dilute acids to liberate hydrogen gas.

stem: A precipitation reaction always produces a(n) __________ product.
solution: A precipitation reaction forms an insoluble solid (precipitate).

stem: The colour of copper sulphate solution fades when an iron nail is dipped in it because __________.
options: iron displaces copper, forming pale green iron sulphate
solution: Iron displaces copper; the blue Cu²⁺ ions are replaced by pale green Fe²⁺ ions.

stem: Which observation indicates that a chemical reaction has occurred?
options: Change in colour, gas evolution or temperature
solution: Colour change, gas evolution, precipitate formation or temperature change signal a chemical reaction.

stem: The dissolving of ammonium chloride in water, which cools the solution, is a(n) __________ process.
solution: Dissolving ammonium chloride absorbs heat, cooling the solution — an endothermic process.

stem: Oil and fat containing food items are flushed with nitrogen because nitrogen is __________.
solution: Nitrogen is unreactive, so it protects food from the oxygen that causes rancidity.

stem: The white precipitate formed when barium chloride reacts with sodium sulphate is __________.
solution: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ + 2NaCl; the white precipitate is barium sulphate.

stem: A reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings is called __________.
solution: Endothermic reactions absorb heat, lowering the temperature of the surroundings.
